summary.prose: The build lays the foundation first: one artifact writer with revisions, then the routing of every existing writer, including the code-review and TESTS records, then the inventory test that locks it in. In parallel it builds the unit issue module for team mode, the per-step extras runner, the legacy and team split of the three approve-time pushes, the draft hook that carries readiness to the author, and finally the lowest-number tie-break, which waits for the findIssues amendment and runs against a fake port until then. The solo regression suite, tracker-auto.test.ts, is never edited.

tasks.title: Add the single artifact writer, the revision field and the widened tracker record
tasks.summary: Add writeArtifact(path, next, kind) and readRevision beside writeAtomic in src/workflow/storage.ts: a content write mints meta.revision (prior + 1, first draft 1) and carries the whole prior meta.tracker block (legacy fields, units, extrasDone) with next winning per key; a meta-only write keeps the on-disk revision; a value without meta throws TypeError. Add the optional revision to ArtifactMetaBase, the optional units to TrackerMeta, UnitRef and UnitIssue types, and widen TrackerMeta.adapter from 'github' to the port's TrackerKind with patchTrackerMeta preserving the actual kind. patchTrackerMeta writes through writeArtifact as meta-only and merges units key by key.
acceptanceChecks: writeArtifact mints revision 1 then +1 on content writes, keeps the revision on meta-only writes, and throws TypeError (file untouched) for a value without meta.
A content write over an existing file keeps every prior tracker field, units and extrasDone, does not carry approvedAt or review, and an artifact with no revision reads as 0.
TrackerMeta.adapter accepts the port's TrackerKind and patchTrackerMeta preserves the kind it is given; every existing tracker field is unchanged.
npx tsc --noEmit passes.

Do not change any artifact body.
acceptanceChecks: appendStoryToDefine mints a revision and keeps the tracker block; approve, reject and ack-stale leave the revision and the body byte-identical.

For each meta-only writer (questions resolution, findings review stamp, refs patch, bugfix stamp, orchestrator tracker push and sync) the body is byte-identical before and after and the revision is unchanged.
The existing tests of these modules pass without edits.

acceptanceChecks: A review that applies auto-fixes bumps the revision and a report-only review does not, through both verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts.
Resolving a finding with apply bumps the revision and accept, override or defer do not.
A first draft written by synthesize or workflow.run has revision 1 and a re-draft keeps the whole prior tracker block.
The existing tests of these modules pass without edits.

tasks.title: Mint revisions on the code-review and TESTS records, with a stated rollback
tasks.summary: Route the code-review json (code-review/runner.ts and the injected writer in code-review-step/handler.ts) and the TESTS json (runners/build/test-record.ts persistTestRecordTask) through writeArtifact as content; their markdown stays an annotated render. Keep the TESTS rollback: restore the prior json bytes (and with them the prior revision) if the document write fails, and when the restore itself also fails, report the possibly inconsistent record state to the caller instead of promising restoration.
acceptanceChecks: A second code review of the same Story and a second persisted test mapping each bump the record's revision, through the runner default writer and the handler's injected writer.
A rolled-back test record (document write fails, restore succeeds) leaves the json bytes and the revision as before.
When both the document write and the json restore fail, the caller is told the record may be inconsistent and a test covers it.
The existing code-review and test-record tests pass without edits.

tasks.summary: Add ARTIFACT_WRITE_INVENTORY (class and via per file; mixed entries name each site and its kind) and the artifact-write-inventory test with a detector that follows direct calls, aliases and injected writers (default parameters and object properties such as write: writeAtomic), with negative and positive controls. Classify every current write site as the LLD states: content, meta-only, mixed, render, record (amendments/store.ts only), migration.
acceptanceChecks: Every production file that calls or passes writeArtifact, writeAtomic, writeFileSync or renameSync has an entry, and a fully migrated file keeps a valid entry.
The detector flags raw writeFileSync, an unannotated raw writeAtomic, 'write: writeAtomic', an alias and a passed writer when none has an entry, and accepts the positive controls.
The classification matches the LLD, including the two code-review files and test-record.ts as content and amendments/store.ts as record.

tasks.title: Build the unit issue module in team mode
tasks.summary: Add src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts: unitLabel, resolveUnitIssueLocal (record then legacy refs with local reconcile), the module-local EnsureResult with phase, ensureUnitIssueDetailed in team mode (local resolve, per-unit label lookup, labels, create with the unit label, link to parent, record at once) with the pre-create and create-phase failure semantics, and ensureUnitIssue as the two-argument PortResult<IssueRef> wrapper. Legacy mode is not built here; tracker-auto keeps its code.
acceptanceChecks: A recorded unit makes no tracker call; a legacy LLD with only storyRef, no units and no unit label creates no second Story issue; a closed issue is adopted.
A failed lookup or label creates nothing and reports phase before-create; a failed create reports phase create and the next call finds the issue by its unit label and creates nothing.
ensureUnitIssue returns PortResult<IssueRef> without a phase and unitLabel gives the three forms, lower-cased, within 50 characters.

tasks.title: Add the team-only extras runner

When the marker write fails after a successful post the next run posts that step again, as the LLD states.
No step goes through bestEffort.

tasks.title: Split tracker-auto into legacy and team mode
tasks.summary: Make autoPushEpicOnHld, autoPushStoryOnLld and autoPushTasksOnPlan read the policy and pick the mode: legacy (policy none or teamMode false) runs today's code exactly, including the per-entry-point extras (the Epic and plan review comments on every push); team mode adopts through ensureUnitIssueDetailed, runs the extras through runUnitExtras, forces Task issues on, and an unreadable policy returns failed. The signatures and the terminal approve call sites stay unchanged.
acceptanceChecks: The existing tracker-auto.test.ts passes with no edit.

In team mode the three pushes adopt draft-created issues and create none, Task issues are created with pushTasks off, a failed Epic lookup returns failed, and an unreadable policy makes all three return failed.
After a draft-created Story issue the first approve runs the Epic task-list splice, the design comment and the review comment once and a second approve posts nothing.
With policy none the gh command sequence and tracker block equal the pre-change ones and pushTasks off still returns skipped.

tasks.title: Add the draft hook and carry readiness through the result types
tasks.summary: Add ensureDraftIssues and IssueReadiness (not-applicable, ready, not-ready with outcomeKnown and the author's message; local-record fast path before loadTracker; Define, HLD, LLD and plan unit lists; Task issues forced; stop at the first failure). Call it right after the draft pair is written in synthesize.ts and in workflow-rpc.ts, and carry issueReadiness and notice on WorkflowStepDone, on RunWorkflowResult (return at line 352) and on the done frame (line 475).
acceptanceChecks: A Define, LLD or plan draft in team mode creates one issue per unit and a second write creates none and runs no command, even with sign-in lost.
An unreachable tracker leaves the draft files, returns not-ready with the reason, and a failed create is worded as unconfirmed, never as no issue.
The emitted workflow.run done frame, RunWorkflowResult and the step result all carry the fields for a team repo and none for a repo without a policy.
A re-draft keeps epicRef, storyRefs and the units, so sync, the chain report and Task approval still work.

tasks.title: Add the lowest-number duplicate tie-break, gated on the findIssues amendment
tasks.summary: Add step 5 of ensureUnitIssueDetailed: after recording, list every issue carrying the unit label through port.findIssues, adopt the lowest-numbered issue, record it in place of its own, comment on and close its own as a duplicate, and keep the created issue when the listing fails. The build starts this task only after the sc1 findIssues amendment (AMD-315d510cb28100e2-10) is agreed with s1; until then it is exercised against a fake port that implements findIssues.
acceptanceChecks: A listing with a lower-numbered issue makes the call adopt it, comment on and close its own; a failing close still adopts.
